issues.title: Bloom filter on first equality key of multi-condition hash joins
issues.hypothesis: Current best q09 plan (JSON profile of q09.m0): lineitem scan (59.99M rows, 2.95s CPU) probes HASH_JOIN with Conditions [l_partkey = p_partkey, l_suppkey = ps_suppkey] whose build side is part⋈partsupp (435,892 rows, ~109K distinct partkeys after contains() filter). The join outputs 3.27M rows (5.4%) but costs 2.84s CPU because all 60M rows are hashed on 2 keys and probed. The lineitem scan only gets min/max dynamic filters (l_partkey>=12 AND <=1999993, l_suppkey 1..100000), which prune nothing. No BF is pushed because JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:775) requires ht->conditions.size()==1, and JoinHashTable::Finalize (join_hashtable.cpp:775-796) feeds the BF the combined multi-column hash. A BF on l_partkey alone would drop ~94% of lineitem rows inside the scan (SelectivityOptionalFilter), shrinking the 2.84s probe to ~0.3s and skipping decode of the other 5 projected columns for dropped rows.
issues.plan: 1) join_hashtable.cpp JoinHashTable::Finalize: when bloom_filter.IsInitialized() and conditions.size() > 1, for each chunk gather key column 0 from the rows (data_collection->Gather(chunk_state.row_locations, *FlatVector::IncrementalSelectionVector(), count, 0 /*first key column*/, key_vec, *FlatVector::IncrementalSelectionVector(), nullptr) with key_vec typed as conditions[0].right->return_type), compute VectorOperations::Hash(key_vec, bf_hashes, count) and bloom_filter.InsertHashes(bf_hashes, count). In InsertHashes, skip the combined-hash BF insert when conditions.size() > 1 (pass a flag or move the BF insert into Finalize). For single-key joins behaviour is unchanged (combined hash == single-column hash). 2) physical_hash_join.cpp CanUseBloomFilter: replace `ht->conditions.size() == 1` with: the filter's condition is HT condition 0 (pass join_condition[filter_idx] from FinalizeFilters, require == 0) and cmp == COMPARE_EQUAL and ht->conditions[0].comparison == COMPARE_EQUAL. PushBloomFilter already uses conditions[0] for key name/type and NullValuesAreEqual(0). Verify ReorderConditions puts equalities first so condition 0 is an equality, and that the HT layout's column 0 is condition 0's key. 3) Keep the existing guards (build_side_has_filter, probe est > HT count, !has_cast, not perfect HT). Add a sqllogictest: 2-key join with filtered build side, check results incl. NULL keys in either column and a build where key0 matches but key1 doesn't.
issues.expected_gain: q09: lineitem HJ 2.84s -> ~0.4s CPU, plus some scan savings; total query CPU ~8.7s -> ~6s, so roughly -20..-30% wall.
issues.generality: Any multi-column equi-join (composite FK, e.g. partsupp-style keys, multi-column joins in star schemas) where the build side is filtered and much smaller than the probe. SelectivityOptionalFilter self-disables when the BF is unselective, so the downside is the extra column gather+hash at HT finalize (proportional to build rows, small) and BF probe on the first few vectors.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Correctness depends on hashing exactly the same column/type the probe-side BFTableFilter hashes; a mismatch drops valid rows. Gather of key 0 for each build chunk must use the right row-location vector. NULL semantics follow existing single-key logic.

dispatch: Bloom filter on first equality key of multi-condition hash joins
output.memory:
# Memory (db_evolve, q09 specialisation run)

## q09 facts after E0001 (gen1 r2, hot ~700ms, 1.417x)
- Plan now: part(contains filter, 109K) -> HJ build with partsupp probe (BF ps_partkey, 460K rows out of 8M) = build side (436K).
  lineitem (60M, scan 2.95s CPU) probes it on 2 keys [l_partkey=p_partkey, l_suppkey=ps_suppkey]: HJ 2.84s CPU, out 3.27M.
  That 3.27M is the build for orders probe (15M rows, HJ 2.37s CPU; orders scan 0.27s, goes through CM compress proj).
  Then supplier⋈nation (tiny), agg 0.2s.
- lineitem scan only gets useless min/max (full range) dynamic filters; no BF since 2-key join.
- orders probe scan has no dynamic filters (compress projection __internal_compress_integral_uinteger(#0,1) blocks pushdown).

## Old (pre-E0001) facts
- Large-build HJs are expensive (~190-300ns/build row): random writes. Small-build HJ probed by 8M rows costs ~0.14s.
- BuildProbeSideOptimizer flip thresholds: orders join flips if left est < ~10M.

## Codebase facts
- JSON profile trick: PRAGMA enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/tmp/x.json'; run query; then
  SELECT unnest(regexp_extract_all(regexp_replace(content,'\s+',' ','g'),'"extra_info": \{[^}]*\}',0)) FROM read_text(...)
  and list_zip of operator_type/operator_timing/operator_cardinality regexes. Shows conditions + dynamic filters per op.
- Don't use `| tail`/cd in dbe-tool bash calls (blocked); use SQL OFFSET instead.
- Optimizer order: STATISTICS_PROPAGATION (adds CM compress projections) runs BEFORE JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN. PushdownJoinFilterExpression passes only colref/integral casts.
- CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:761): needs ht->conditions.size()==1, EQUAL, build_side_has_filter, probe est > ht count, not perfect HT. BF deferred to HT finalize.
- BF filled in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes (join_hashtable.cpp:717) from combined hash loaded from row layout in Finalize (:775). PushBloomFilter uses ht.conditions[0].
- FinalizeFilters loops filter_idx over join_condition; min/max pushed per condition.
- BF = 12 bits/key; in-scan via SelectivityOptionalFilter (self-disables if unselective).

## Plan of attack
1. DONE E0001 contains() selectivity: -29%.
2. (dispatched r2) BF on first equality key of multi-key joins -> lineitem 60M -> ~3.3M. Expect -20..-30%.
3. Next: push join filters through CM compress projections -> BF on o_orderkey for the orders probe (15M -> 3.3M, HJ 2.37s). Issue in backlog.
4. Then agg (0.2s) / projections (0.18s compress string proj) are small.

## Exhausted / retired
(none yet)
